items.title: Chico Hamilton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lionel heard me one night and he offered me the job on his band... I went on the band. I lasted three weeks

ctx.x: I was about eight or nine years old. And funny thing, not a funny thing, but Lionel Hampton was, you know, from LA and I’d see him at the Lincoln Theater. And Lionel would take the sticks and play all over the floor, and the wall, and all over and I imitated -- I could do that. I’d imitate Lionel, right? So when we were in junior high school there was a piano player by the name of Chooie Reyes. He was a piano player who later became a Mexican piano player who later became very famous. His name was Chooie Reyes.…

items.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000
items.q: Lionel Hampton was very popular at that time you know. ... So I used to imitate him.

ctx.x: As a matter of fact he’s totally responsible I guess for me getting into music because his folks gave him a clarinet when he was around that age. So he being my best friend, I had to have a clarinet. And we were so poor though, we couldn’t afford, you could get a clarinet from the school for two dollars a semester. And it took us, man it must have took me about a whole semester to get two dollars together. But anyway, getting back to that, Lionel Hampton was very popular at that time you know.
